1. Open Device center on the Android device running Local Signage.

2. Connect the display and your phone or computer to the same local network. You can also start the device hotspot and connect the controller to it.

3. Scan the QR code on a phone. On a computer, open the local address shown on the display and enter the six-digit computer pairing code. Temporary pairing credentials refresh periodically.

4. After the browser connects, open Send, choose content, and start playback. Content stored on the display can continue playing when the internet is unavailable.

Send content from the Web console on a phone or computer. The controller does not need a dedicated app.

Text: enter text and choose the font, size, colors, background, and ticker speed.

Images: choose photos or files, or add HTTPS image addresses. Fit, fill, crop, and stretch modes are available.

Video: choose a local video or HTTPS video address, then set display fit and playback speed.

Live: enter an HLS, DASH, or RTSP address. The display connects directly to the source.

Web: enter an HTTPS page address and optionally set a refresh interval.

After a successful send, the content is stored on the current display and a basic playback configuration is created automatically. Full playback controls are on the Playback page.

HTML labels create fully styled screens for notices, promotions, menus, and status boards. They are separate from plain text content.

Steps:

1. Open Send in the Web console and choose HTML.

2. Choose a notice, promotion, or status-board template, or enter your own HTML and CSS.

3. Check the result in the preview area.

4. Select Send and play.

HTML plays as the full primary screen. It does not overlay images, video, or plain text. Scripts, external assets, and embedded pages are blocked for offline reliability and security.

The Playback page in the Web console provides play, pause, stop, previous, next, mute, and volume controls, together with current content and runtime status.

The display playback screen stays minimal. Tap the screen to temporarily show Device center and pause or resume controls.

Display fit, keep-awake, startup resume, and fullscreen options are under the current-device settings in the Web console. Settings are stored on the display and remain active after restart.

Multi-device features work on the same local network and do not require a cloud account.

1. Open Devices in the Web console.

2. Add another discovered display and enter the pairing token shown by that target device.

3. After pairing, review each device’s online state, current content, and playback state.

4. Open a target device to choose different saved content, sync and play content, or control playback, mute, and volume independently.

One offline device does not stop other devices from continuing playback.

No QR code: confirm that the device is connected by Wi-Fi or Ethernet, or start its hotspot, then wait for a local address.

The browser cannot open the console: confirm that both devices are on the same local network. Disable VPN or guest-network isolation that may block local traffic.

Image or video send fails: check the file type, file size, and free storage on the display.

Live playback fails: verify the address, use HLS, DASH, or RTSP, and confirm that the display network can reach the source.

HTML cannot be sent: remove scripts, external resources, and embedded pages, then try again.

For continuing issues, review recent operations and playback errors on the Records page in the Web console.

Purchases must be completed on the Android phone, tablet, or signage device where Local Signage is installed. The local Web console never handles payment.

A seven-day full local trial starts after the first successful launch and never charges automatically. Playback continues after the trial with a Trial ended label.

Open Plans and license from Device center on the Android device to choose the Google Play annual subscription or one-time lifetime version. Google Play provides the final price and currency.

To restore an existing purchase, use the same Google Play account and select Restore purchases. Manage or cancel an annual subscription under Payments and subscriptions in Google Play. Uninstalling the app does not cancel a subscription.
